content.intro: Print a Farkle score sheet with the scoring chart, or keep the running totals on your phone. The first to 10,000 sets up the final round.
howToUse: Write each player's name at the top of a column. After every turn, write the points that player banked in their next empty box, or a zero if they farkled. Add each new score to the player's running total as you go.

Many tables say you need at least 500 points in a single turn before you can bank anything for the first time. When someone's total passes 10,000, every other player gets one last turn to beat it, and the highest total wins.
On a phone, tap a box on the sheet to write a turn. The sheet keeps the totals, reminds you about the 500-point opening rule, and tells you when the final round has started.

faqs.q: How many points do you need to win Farkle?
faqs.a: 10,000 is the most common target. Once a player passes it, everyone else gets one more turn to beat that total, and the highest score wins.
A roll with no scoring dice in it: no 1s, no 5s and no scoring combinations. You lose every point you collected that turn and pass the dice.

faqs.q: Do you need 500 points to get on the board?
faqs.a: Many tables play that way: your first banked score must be at least 500 from a single turn. Some play with 350, some with no minimum, so agree before you start.
If every one of your six dice has scored, you may pick them all up and roll again, adding to the points you already have this turn.

faqs.q: Is there a penalty for three farkles in a row?
faqs.a: At some tables, yes: a player who farkles on three turns in a row loses 1,000 points. It is a house rule, so check with your group.

faqs.q: How many people can play Farkle?
faqs.a: Two or more. The printable sheet has six columns and the online scorekeeper takes up to eight players.
